I'm not sure where to start. It feels like I've been dragging myself through treacle for the past year.  Just... sad, I guess. Everything feels heavy, and even simple things like talking to my wife or catching up with colleagues just seem like too much effort. I'm always tired, no matter how much I rest. Honestly, there have been times – especially recently – where I felt like the only way to get this feeling to stop was to... well, to just stop everything. I’ve even started looking up things online, just out of curiosity, about how someone might go about it.

Before all this, though, about a month ago, it was really different. I had so much energy, felt on top of the world. My team actually struggled to keep up with me. I barely slept but felt completely refreshed, ready to tackle anything. My speech would get really fast, and I found myself jumping from one idea to the next. My wife even mentioned how much more… affectionate I was becoming. I’d be constantly moving, pacing during calls, having to do something with my hands. It was like I was buzzing. Now, that energy is just gone, and this exhaustion has settled back in.
D009-D003_h001.question_a:
I'm here because things have been pretty chaotic, especially lately. For about a month now, I’ve been on this high. I feel fantastic, full of energy, and just... euphoric. I barely sleep, maybe an hour or two a night, but I don't feel tired at all. In fact, I've been tackling so many projects at work, almost too many, and my team can barely keep up with my ideas. My wife says I've been talking a mile a minute, jumping from one topic to another, and she can't get a word in edgewise. And honestly, my sex drive has gone through the roof. It’s been great, actually, I feel incredibly productive, and it hasn’t caused any real problems, just feeling really upbeat.

But that’s not the whole story. Before this burst of energy, and for about a year before that, I was absolutely miserable. I felt this profound sadness that I just couldn't shake. I pulled away from everyone, didn't want to see friends, and even family felt like too much effort. I was constantly exhausted, no matter how much I rested, and it affected my work performance significantly. There was even a point when I was so low, I tried to end things, which is what really scared me enough to seek help. It's like these periods of being on top of the world, with all this rapid speech and boundless energy, only happen when I'm in one of these "highs." Outside of that, I feel completely different.
D009-D003_h001.question_b:
"Honestly, doctor, I'm feeling pretty low right now. It's been going on for about a year, this constant sadness that just clings to me. I used to enjoy going out with my wife and friends, but now I just want to be left alone. Even after a full night's sleep, I wake up feeling completely drained, like I haven't rested at all. There have been times, especially recently, where things just felt so bleak I found myself thinking about ending it all, even looking up ways to do it.

What's really confusing is that it's not always like this. About a month ago, I had this burst of energy. I felt absolutely fantastic, full of unmotivated happiness, and just couldn't sit still. I'd bounce from one task to another, feeling like I barely needed any sleep – maybe 2 or 3 hours a night, and I'd be ready to go. My wife kept telling me I was talking a mile a minute, jumping from one idea to the next, and she could barely keep up. I even found myself pursuing more sexual activities, which is unusual for me. During that time, I was incredibly productive at work, my team even commented on how much I was getting done. But these periods of heightened energy and fast talking, along with needing less sleep, they’re not new to me, not just a recent thing. They've been a part of who I am, on and off, since I was a kid, well before I even started high school. It’s always been there, even when I’m not feeling particularly ‘up’ like last month, I still struggle with that inner restlessness and quick thinking most days."

I even started taking on extra shifts, driving almost constantly, trying to maximize my earnings. My ex-wife kept calling about the bills, but I figured I’d pay them off with my new earnings. I made some big purchases too, like a new sound system for the car and a top-of-the-line coffee machine, thinking it would make me feel even better and help with the long hours. During this time, my thoughts were racing, and I found myself talking a mile a minute, jumping from one idea to the next. I barely needed any sleep; a few hours felt like enough, and I was still buzzing.

But then, the other side of the seesaw hit, and for the last two months, I’ve been in a deep hole. It's like a heavy blanket has been thrown over me, and I can't shake this persistent sadness. Sleep became a problem again, but this time it was the opposite – not restless energy, but unsettling nightmares almost every night. I’d wake up in a cold sweat, images of crashing the taxi or losing everything vivid in my mind. It’s hard to even get out of bed most days, let alone drive. It’s tough to focus on anything, and I’m definitely not taking on extra shifts anymore. My boss has actually called me in a few times, asking why I’m missing days.
